newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-CONTROVERSIAL FERNANDEZ MAKES ATHLETIC LIONS ROAR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CONTROVERSIAL FERNANDEZ MAKES ATHLETIC LIONS ROAR.

text.p: Former Paris St Germain coach Luis Fernandez has injected new life into Athletic Bilbao, the fallen giants of Spanish soccer and one of only three sides never to have been relegated.
But Fernandez's aggressive touch-line style -- on show for all to see during his side's 2-1 victory over Barcelona last month -- has been widely criticised by rival clubs.
Fernandez, 37, has lost none of the tenacity and doggedness that made him the ideal foil to stylish midfielder Michel Platini in the unforgettable French side of the mid 1980s.
"I still feel like a player," says Fernandez, who ran on to the pitch and was close to throwing himself on top of a pile of players celebrating Athletic's equaliser against Barcelona.
In an earlier excursion from the coaching area he exchanged words with Barcelona reserve coach Jose Mourinho. Fernandez's final sortie from the bench earned him a yellow card.
In the week leading up to the game the Athletic coach had stoked up the tension with a series of verbal attacks against his opponents. And the war of words continued after the match in the tunnel.
"Now you can dive," Fernandez said to Luis Figo, whom he had previously accused of faking penalties, before coming close to blows with both Figo and Barcelona midfielder Josep Guardiola.
Fernandez was severely rebuked by Barcelona general manager Jaume Pares.
"He's rude and disgraceful," said Pares.
Not surprisingly Athletic president Jose Maria Arrate had better things to say about his new signing.
"I believe his character forms a decisive part in his success," Arrate said. "He's a fundamental part in the resurrection of Athletic...he's restored optimism to the club."
Optimism has been running in short supply at Athletic in recent years.
One of the oldest sides in Spain, only Athletic, Real Madrid and Barcelona have been ever-present in the first division since the inaugural 1928-29 season.
By that stage Athletic had already won nine of their record 23 Spanish Cups.
But the trophy cupboard has been bare since the double-winning 1983-84 season, and Athletic have qualified only twice for Europe in a decade in which Real and Barcelona have dominated.
But Athletic have been at a disadvantage in competing with the multi-billion peseta galaxy of international stars fielded by the Spanish game's 'old firm'.

The club have maintained their policy of not accepting sponsorship. Nor do Athletic sign players born outside the Basque country, which accounts for some of the characteristically Basque names of the current squad -- Etxeberria, Bidaurrazaga, Mendiguren, Goikoetxea, Larrainzar and Tabuenka.

The policy has strengthened Athletic's status as a potent symbol of Basque nationalism but their recent fall from grace has prompted speculation that the regulation will be scrapped in 1998, the club's centennial year.
The rumours increased over the summer after the rules were stretched to sign Bixente Lizarazu, who was born over the border in French Basque Country.
Neighbours Real Sociedad of San Sebastian have already made the move and now sign foreign players, while still barring non-Basque Spaniards.
Athletic have the same rule but only for coaches.

And the arrival of another French citizen has restored Athletic's faith in keeping their traditions alive. Despite his origins in the southern Spanish town of Tarifa, the Fernandez family's subsequent move to France ensured Luis a French passport.
Fernandez's hands were full upon his return to Spain, as he inherited a side which came perilously close to relegation.
His solutions, however, have not been to everybody's liking.
Fernandez has banned the media from training sessions and players have been unable to choose room mates for away games.
The revolution has coincided with the appointment of Sabino Padilla as team doctor.
Padilla, who numbers cyclist Miguel Indurain and world marathon champion Martin Fiz among his clients, has made radical changes to the diet of the Athletic players.
Midfielder Julen Guerrero has lost weight and rediscovered his goal touch and, as part of a five-man attack, has been instrumental in leading the team known as the Lions to fifth place in the league.
"The Lions no longer look like lambs," commented one sports columnist recently.
